data.narrative:
Charge Robotics is a Series B-stage housing and construction robotics company founded by Banks Hunter and Max Justicz. The target operates within a four-company private comparable set (Plantd Materials, Cuby Technologies, Cover, and Somos); no public comps exist in this subsector, limiting direct market-based benchmarking.

The valuation analysis employs stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $44M as a baseline value proxy, a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage financing rounds yields an implied valuation of $83M. This reflects the expected value creation between funding stages absent revenue multiples or comparable transaction data.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $71M to $96M, with $83M as the median. The range reflects typical upside/downside variance around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the absence of public comps and limited visibility into the private peer set's recent valuations, financing terms, and operational performance. Revenue trajectory, customer concentration, and technology differentiation within the housing robotics sector represent material valuation drivers not quantifiable from available data. Additional comparable transaction data or disclosure of revenue metrics would materially refine this range.
